title: REAP-guided engineering improves P450 BM3 activity
summary: REAP combines a protein-language-model ranking predictor with active selection and automated build-and-test cycles. The study reports a P450 BM3 quintuple variant with 57-fold higher product yield than the engineered FL#62 starting scaffold in its high-throughput assay. This is a variant-specific comparison with an already engineered scaffold, not a 57-fold gain over wild type. A separate sortase result is not covered here.

evidence.tested: Publisher indexed article reports a quintuple variant and 57-fold product-yield increase over FL#62 in the high-throughput assay; kinetic characterization is also described.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and broader application are not established by this bounded review.
evidence.ai_role: Learned ranking and active selection nominate variants for automated synthesis and testing; the reported gain is measured against the engineered FL#62 scaffold.

source_review.scope: Publisher indexed primary article text, title/DOI and result; PMC direct open CAPTCHA challenged. Journal/preprint chronology and sequence overlap not audited.
